info.name: HRM - Employee Onboarding (Invite → Approval)
info.description:
Invite Employee flow: Company Admin invites a new hire (optionally with access_role_id — their permission role, staged until activation and shown read-only to the employee), the hire self-services their pre-boarding via a token link (no password yet), Admin reviews/approves-or-rejects documents, then activates the employee (creates their login and emails credentials).

Invite links expire after 30 minutes (ONBOARDING_INVITE_EXPIRES_MINUTES, default 30). Once expired, GET/PATCH /me return 401 with `code: "token_expired"`. The employee does NOT get a new link directly at that point — they call 7b (Request New Invite Link): if the previous invite is actually still valid it's rejected with `code: "invite_still_valid"`; otherwise HR/whoever invited them (employees.invited_by) gets an email, and an admin must explicitly call 4 (Resend Invite) to actually issue + send the new link.

Run order: 0) Login as Company Admin → 1) Invite Employee → 7) employee self-service using {{onboarding_token}} → [if expired: 7b, then admin re-runs 4, then retry 7] → 8-10) fill profile/documents/dependants → 11) Submit → 2/3) Admin review → 5a/5b) Approve/Reject documents → 6) Activate.

Set `base_url` before running (default assumes local dev on port 3002).

request.description: Convenience login to obtain a Company Admin Bearer token. Fills admin_token and company_id automatically.

body.raw:
{
  "first_name": "Bilal",
  "last_name": "Ahmed",
  "personal_email": "bilal.ahmed@example.com",
  "work_email": "",
  "phone_number": "+923211234567",
  "employee_code": "MTU-2026-042",
  "designation_id": null,
  "department_id": null,
  "employee_type_id": null,
  "work_location_id": null,
  "shift_id": null,
  "joining_date": "2026-04-15",
  "line_manager_id": null,
  "access_role_id": {{access_role_id}}
}

request.description:
Only first_name, last_name, personal_email, employee_code are required. designation/department accept free-text strings instead of the _id fields too. work_email is optional — leave blank and it defaults to personal_email, so the employee record always has a usable email (matches how Add Employee-created employees look). Response includes a top-level `email` field too (work_email falling back to personal_email) for consistency with GET /employees.

access_role_id is optional — the permission role Company Admin assigns at invite time. There's no `users` row yet (no login exists until activation), so it's staged on employee_job_details and returned read-only to the employee under official.access_role_id / official.access_role_name in GET /employee-onboarding/me and GET /employees/:id. The employee can never edit it (PATCH /me never touches it). At activation (step 6) it's copied onto the new users.access_role_id so the permission actually takes effect on login. Response also echoes access_role_id / access_role_name back for confirmation.

No separate onboarding list endpoint — the existing GET /employees now surfaces invited/pre-boarding employees too. `status` accepts active, inactive, pending, pending_invite, or pre_boarding. Each employee in the response also carries an onboarding_status field, and official.access_role_id / official.access_role_name (falls back to the staged invite-time value until activation, same as the detail endpoints).

item.name: 3. Get Onboarding Employee By Id (submission detail)

request.description: This one stays a dedicated endpoint (unlike listing) — it returns the document checklist with approve/reject state and skip reasons (onboarding_documents[]), which the plain GET /employees/:id detail view doesn't include. It also returns documents[] (the merged Add-Employee-style view, which now includes onboarding uploads too, tagged source: "onboarding").

The only step that actually generates a new token/link and emails it to the employee — resending is always an explicit Company Admin action. Normally called after receiving the "X requested a new onboarding invite link" email triggered by 7b, but can be called any time. Resets invited_at, restarting the 30-minute validity window.

Leave work_email blank to use personal_email as the login. Fails until the employee has submitted (pre_boarding) and no document is stuck in rejected. Also copies the access_role_id staged at invite time (step 1) onto the new users row, so the permission role actually takes effect.

Returns the full profile — personal, official (access_role_id/access_role_name read-only), salary, documents[] (now includes onboarding uploads too, alongside any employee_profile/hr_request docs — check the source field), dependants[], employee_bank, and the separate onboarding_documents[] checklist (approval status/skip/rejection reasons).

If the token has expired (30 min after it was issued), this returns 401 with `code: "token_expired"` — go to 7b instead of retrying this.

item.name: 7b. Request New Invite Link (after token expires)

request.description:
Call this once 7 starts returning `code: "token_expired"` — send the same (now-expired) token here; it's only used to identify who's asking, not required to still be valid.

This never returns a new link directly:
- If the previous invite is actually still within its 30-minute window → 409 with `code: "invite_still_valid"` ("You already have a valid, active invite link...").
- If it's genuinely expired → 200 ("Your request for a new invite link has been submitted...") and an email goes to whoever invited the employee (employees.invited_by). They then have to explicitly run 4 (Resend Invite) to actually issue and send the new link — grab the fresh token from that response and update {{onboarding_token}} before continuing.

request.description:
All four sections — personal, employee_bank, documents, dependants — are independently optional; only the ones present in the body are touched. No official/designation/department/salary/access_role_id fields here — those stay Company Admin-only (see step 1).

employee_bank aliases: employeeBank, bank_details, employee_bank_details, bank all also accepted.

documents: array, multiple entries in one call, upserted one by one against onboarding_documents keyed by document_type_id. Each entry is either { document_type_id, file_url, file_name } or { document_type_id, skip: true, skip_reason } to skip a mandatory doc with a reason. Get file_url from 9a first. This does the same thing as 9b/9c, just inline and batched — 9b/9c still work standalone too.

dependants: array, multiple entries, replaces the full dependant list each call. Pass an existing id (or {"id": ...}) to keep one, or an object with full_name/phone_no/relationship (no id) to create a brand-new dependant inline — this is the only way that actually works during onboarding: POST /dependants (step 10a) requires a real login Bearer token (userId+email claims), which the onboarding_token doesn't have, so it 401s if called directly here.
Public endpoint, no Authorization needed. Pick a file for the 'image' form field (images or PDFs both accepted here).

Upsert keyed by document_type_id — calling again replaces the prior file/skip and clears any rejection. One document per call — step 8's documents[] array does the same thing but for multiple documents in one request.

item.name: 10a. Create Dependant (does NOT work with onboarding_token — see note)

request.description: NOTE: despite looking public, this route is gated by protect('dependants','add') → requireAuth, which needs a real login JWT carrying userId + email. The onboarding_token (only {employeeId, companyId, purpose}) does NOT satisfy that and will 401 here. During onboarding, don't use this step — create dependants inline instead via step 8's dependants[] array (objects with full_name/phone_no/relationship, no id needed, multiple at once). This endpoint is kept here for reference / for flows that already hold a real Company Admin or logged-in login token (e.g. admin managing dependants directly).

item.name: 10b. Attach Dependants To My Profile (existing ids only)

request.description: Replaces the full dependant list each call — include every id you want kept. Only takes ids (of dependants that already exist), so it's only useful once a dependant already has an id (e.g. from an admin-side flow). For onboarding self-service, prefer step 8's dependants[] array, which can create brand-new dependants inline in the same call and also replaces the full list.
Fails 400 with a missing_documents list if any mandatory document type has no upload/skip yet, or is still rejected.
